reports.title: Gross domestic product (quarterly)
reports.description: Stats NZ's quarterly GDP information release, New Zealand's official measure of economic activity, compiled per the 'Quarterly gross domestic product: Sources and methods' (fifth edition). The quarterly series is benchmarked annually to annual accounts whose industry data comes largely from the Annual Enterprise Survey: the sources-and-methods document states that new annual data is incorporated once a year at the September-quarter release. Minted as the corpus's representative of the 'national accounts' family the AES metadata names as its principal consumer; the legacy product titles that metadata lists (Production/Industry Accounts, Institutional Sector Accounts, Inter-Industry Study, Provisional National Accounts) are predecessors of the current GDP and national-accounts release set.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly, roughly 11 weeks after the reference quarter. Annual benchmark data is incorporated once a year: "The new annual data is incorporated into the quarterly accounts once a year for the September quarter information release, published in December."

release_schedule.note: Stats NZ's release calendar (filter by month = September 2026) lists '17 Sep Gross domestic product: June 2026 quarter'. This is consistent with the on-file cadence_note (quarterly, ~11 weeks after reference quarter end). The most recently published edition was the March 2026 quarter, released 18 June 2026.

reports.title: Regional gross domestic product
reports.description: Stats NZ's annual geographic breakdown of national GDP by region and industry, published for years ended March. Its own introduction page states, in one sentence, all four of its main inputs by name: the Annual Enterprise Survey, Linked Employer-Employee Data, the Crown Financial Information System, and the Local Authority Census — two of which are already nodes in this corpus, making this the most efficiently documented node in the New Zealand slice.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, for years ended March; editions verified for 2016, 2018, 2022 and 2024.

entries.covers: Regional gross domestic product: Year ended March 2026

release_schedule.note: Stats NZ's page for the 'Year ended March 2025' edition (published 24 March 2026) states under 'Next release': 'Regional gross domestic product: Year ended March 2026 will be released in March 2027.' Only month-level precision is given, not an exact day. This confirms the annual, ~12-month-after-fiscal-year-end cadence already noted in the corpus's cadence_note.

reports.title: Tourism satellite account
reports.description: Stats NZ's annual satellite account measuring tourism's contribution to the New Zealand economy. Its DataInfo+ metadata describes it as providing "a picture of the role tourism plays in New Zealand, with information on the changing levels and impact of tourism activity", published annually. Its published methodology derives industry output and scales household tourism expenditure using Annual Enterprise Survey data, which is the edge that brought it into this corpus.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, for years ended March; the 2025 edition (year ended March 2025) is current.

entries.covers: Tourism satellite account: Year ended March 2026

release_schedule.note: Stats NZ's own release page for the current edition (year ended March 2025, published 03 March 2026) states verbatim: 'Next release: Tourism satellite account: Year ended March 2026 will be released in 2027.' No specific month/day is given, only the year, so precision is set to 'year'.

reports.title: Non-profit institutions satellite account
reports.description: Stats NZ's periodic satellite account of the non-profit sector's contribution to GDP, supplementing the New Zealand System of National Accounts. Three editions exist — for the 2004 year (published 2007), 2013 and 2018 — which the 2018 edition itself confirms: "the NPISA, first published in 2007 and presenting statistics for the 2004 year". The weakest recurrence claim among this pass's nodes, held as a node because the editions form a deliberate series with cross-edition comparisons rather than a one-off.
reports.cadence_note: Irregular: editions for 2004, 2013 and 2018, roughly every five to nine years. releases_per_year is nominal.

release_schedule.note: Stats NZ's Non-profit institutions satellite account (NPISA) page (2018 edition, published 2020-03-27) has no 'next release' date, no related release-calendar entry, and no stated periodicity rule anywhere in the page's structured content. Only three editions have ever been published (2004, 2013, 2018), each covering the NZ System of National Accounts year roughly 5-9 years apart. As of 2026-08-11 no 2019-2026 edition exists at the expected URL pattern (checked non-profit-institutions-satellite-account-{2019..2025}, all 404), and Stats NZ's release calendar has no NPISA entry, confirming this remains genuinely unscheduled/irregular rather than on any fixed or statutory cadence.

reports.title: Business price indexes
reports.description: Stats NZ's quarterly producer-side price release. Its DataInfo+ metadata states: "The BPI release includes the PPI, CGPI, and farm expenses price index (FEPI)." The PPI measures output and input price change for industries, the CGPI capital goods prices. Named by exact title in the AES's own metadata as a consumer of AES data, but no product-side document reachable this session corroborates that (see _dropped); the node instead anchors a documented inbound edge from the quarterly GDP release, whose sources-and-methods uses PPI sub-indexes for inventory revaluation.

release_schedule.note: Stats NZ does not publish a long-range dated calendar reachable via automated fetch (release-calendar page is JS-rendered), and no explicit 'next release' statement was found on individual release pages via fetch. However, past editions show a very consistent quarterly pattern: released on/around the 18th-20th of the second month after quarter-end -- March 2025 quarter released 19 May 2025; June 2025 quarter released ~19 Aug 2025; September 2025 quarter released 19-20 Nov 2025; December 2025 quarter released 18-19 Feb 2026; March 2026 quarter released 19 May 2026. Projecting forward, the June 2026 quarter release is expected around 19 August 2026 and the September 2026 quarter release around 19 November 2026.

reports.title: New Zealand Standard Industrial Output Classification (NZSIOC)
reports.description: The New Zealand-only output classification layered on top of ANZSIC 2006, and the level at which Stats NZ actually designs its business surveys and compiles the national accounts -- "NZSIOC is an output view of the ANZSIC classification designed for the production of aggregated industry statistics" (Stats NZ to the UN Committee of Experts on ISIC, 2022). Four hierarchical levels: Level 1, "16 categories at this level. They match with the ANZSIC division level, except for three categories which combine two divisions together"; Level 2, "31 categories at this level which generally match with the ANZSIC division level, except that agriculture and manufacturing are split"; Level 3, "55 categories at this level. This level generally matches an ANZSIC subdivision or consists of several smaller subdivisions combined together"; Level 4, "118 working industries" where the National Accounts are compiled. Stats NZ built it because ANZSIC 2006's structure "does not always mirror the New Zealand economy" -- specifically, "because of the significance of agriculture and its downstream industries, users require more information about agriculture and primary food product manufacturing than what is provided at the ANZSIC group level". TITLE VARIANT, on file so it is not rediscovered: Stats NZ's own 2010 implementation paper expands the acronym as "New Zealand Standard Industry Output Categories", while its 2022 and 2025 papers to UN classification bodies and the Annual Enterprise Survey's DataInfo+ metadata use "New Zealand Standard Industrial Output Classification". The later and more widely used form is taken as the title here. MINTED 2026-08-09 on Thomas's ruling, after a cheap-check pass established that NZSIOC has no defining publication of its own -- no edition, no catalogue number, no version -- and is distributed as downloadable classification tables. Three Stats NZ-authored sources describe it and none names a founding instrument; Stats NZ's 2022 UN paper says outright that NZSIOC "was created as an afterthought" whose "purpose and/or need was not actually considered during the ANZSIC06 review". The ruling was that `Research.1.md` sec.4's bar is named + titled, which NZSIOC meets, and that the volumes `anzsic` and `isic` happen to have were never a requirement.
reports.cadence_note: Evergreen; `releases_per_year` deliberately absent, per sec.4's one-off foundational-instrument shape and the precedent of `eu-reg-2016-2304`. There is no observed revision interval to derive a rate from: NZSIOC has no published edition sequence at all. Forward-looking caveat from Stats NZ's 2025 ECLAC workshop paper -- "There has been no review of ANZSIC since the commencement of the revision in 2006 and it is heavily out of date and difficult to use", and New Zealand is "contemplating adopting ISIC Rev 5 either as is or with a few minor class adjustments" -- so NZSIOC's parent may be replaced rather than revised, which would force a decision about this node rather than a routine update.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY BY THIS SESSION (2026-08-09) from two Stats NZ papers in the Stats NZ digital library (statsnz.contentdm.oclc.org, collection p20045coll1), both fetched in full. 'ANZSIC 2006 implementation: Progress at January 2010' (id 1430): Statistics New Zealand developed NZSIOC "using the principles used to derive ANZSIC categories - organisation of units, industry homogeneity, and economic significance - but adapted specifically to the New Zealand situation", and "To maintain consistency with ANZSIC and ISIC, the ANZSIC ordering and structure has not been broken unless absolutely necessary." 'Introducing ANZSIC 2006' (id 1394) states each NZSIOC level as an aggregation of named ANZSIC levels -- Level 1 categories "match with the ANZSIC division level, except for three categories which combine two divisions together"; Level 3 "generally matches an ANZSIC subdivision or consists of several smaller subdivisions combined together". Corroborated by Stats NZ's 2022 paper to the UN Committee of Experts on ISIC: "Stats NZ uses the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial 2006 (ANZSIC06) as the framework...supplemented through the use of the New Zealand Standard Industrial Output Classification (NZSIOC)", and its 2025 ECLAC workshop paper: ANZSIC "Is supported by an output classification (NZSIOC)". Typed `methodology_depends_on`, not `calculated_from`: NZSIOC is built by aggregating ANZSIC categories under stated principles, not computed from ANZSIC output. NOT trap 5a -- "To maintain consistency with ANZSIC" would be a comparability claim on its own, but the derivation sentence (built using ANZSIC's own principles, structure not broken) is a construction claim.

RULED AND MINTED 2026-08-09 (Thomas, this session): named + titled is the bar sec.4 actually sets; `anzsic` and `isic` happen to have volumes but sec.4 never required one. `nz-nzsioc` is minted in this file as an evergreen node with no `releases_per_year`, together with both edges the entry proposed. Entry closed. UPDATED 2026-08-09 (cheap-check pass, later session same day as the long-tail sweep): the blocker has changed shape and is no longer access. DataInfo+ remains robots-disallowed to this session's fetch tooling in both /Item/ and /item/ casings, and archive.stats.govt.nz no longer resolves at all (DNS failure, not robots) -- so the metadata item behind the earlier 'one successful fetch closes this' claim is still unread. But three further Stats NZ-authored sources were fetched successfully this session and between them make the defining-document question answerable in the negative. (a) Stats NZ, 'ANZSIC 2006 implementation: Progress at January 2010' (Stats NZ digital library, statsnz.contentdm.oclc.org, p20045coll1 id 1430, fetched this session): NZSIOC was created because ANZSIC 2006's structure "does not always mirror the New Zealand economy" -- "because of the significance of agriculture and its downstream industries, users require more information about agriculture and primary food product manufacturing than what is provided at the ANZSIC group level" -- and Statistics NZ developed it "using the principles used to derive ANZSIC categories - organisation of units, industry homogeneity, and economic significance - but adapted specifically to the New Zealand situation", with "To maintain consistency with ANZSIC and ISIC, the ANZSIC ordering and structure has not been broken unless absolutely necessary." (b) Stats NZ, 'Introducing ANZSIC 2006' (same digital library, id 1394, fetched this session): the four levels stated in full -- Level 1 "16 categories at this level. They match with the ANZSIC division level, except for three categories which combine two divisions together"; Level 2 "31 categories at this level which generally match with the ANZSIC division level, except that agriculture and manufacturing are split"; Level 3 "55 categories at this level. This level generally matches an ANZSIC subdivision or consists of several smaller subdivisions combined together"; Level 4 "118 working industries" where the National Accounts are compiled. (c) Stats NZ's own paper to the 2022 UN Committee of Experts on ISIC (UNCEISC 2022, Session 3c, 'New Zealand ANZSIC-ISIC Issues', unstats.un.org, fetched this session): "NZSIOC is an output view of the ANZSIC classification designed for the production of aggregated industry statistics", and "Stats NZ uses the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial 2006 (ANZSIC06) as the framework...supplemented through the use of the New Zealand Standard Industrial Output Classification (NZSIOC)" -- and, notably against the existence of any founding instrument, that NZSIOC "was created as an afterthought" whose "purpose and/or need was not actually considered during the ANZSIC06 review". NONE of the three names a defining publication, an edition, a catalogue number or a version for NZSIOC; all three describe it as a set of categories Stats NZ publishes as downloadable classification tables (Excel) alongside the releases that use it. The working conclusion is that NZSIOC has no front matter to read, rather than that this session failed to find it -- which converts the blocker from access to a node-rule question. That question is Thomas's and is flagged for him rather than decided here: does a classification with a title, a documented derivation and a documented structure, but no defining publication of its own, qualify under `Research.1.md` sec.4 on the same footing as `anzsic` (catalogue no. 1292.0, signed Preface) and `isic` (numbered revisions), both of which do have volumes? Left `deferred` pending that ruling rather than minted, per sec.3. Second, a naming discrepancy worth not rediscovering: Stats NZ's own 2010 implementation paper expands NZSIOC as 'New Zealand Standard Industry Output Categories', while its 2022 and 2025 UN papers and the AES DataInfo+ item expand it as 'New Zealand Standard Industrial Output Classification'. Both expansions are Stats NZ's own usage; if the node is minted, the title field needs a decision on which is current. Third, forward-looking and relevant to cadence if it is minted: Stats NZ's 2025 ECLAC workshop paper states "There has been no review of ANZSIC since the commencement of the revision in 2006 and it is heavily out of date and difficult to use" and that New Zealand is "contemplating adopting ISIC Rev 5 either as is or with a few minor class adjustments" -- so NZSIOC's parent may be replaced rather than revised, and NZSIOC itself has no observed revision interval to derive a `releases_per_year` from. The NZSIOC DataInfo+ item (nz.govt.stats/0381a627-927b-4d60-bce3-bba549bf5a2d) was located but datainfoplus.stats.govt.nz, after serving three items early in this session, began returning robots-disallowed for every URL in both /Item/ and /item/ casings, including robots.txt itself; the data.govt.nz catalogue mirror is behind Incapsula. G.4's 'DataInfo+ is fetchable' should be read as 'intermittently fetchable'. What was obtained instead, from Stats NZ's own presentation to the 2025 UN ECLAC classifications workshop (Andrew Hancock, 'Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC)', unstats.un.org, fetched this session): ANZSIC "Is supported by an output classification (NZSIOC) and forms the basis of the Business Industry Classification (BIC)"; "In the New Zealand context it has become a minor input classification as NZSIOC is used for sample survey design and all outputs"; "In addition to assist implementation, a separate New Zealand Standard Industrial Output Classification (NZSIOC) was created for all aggregated data such as working or published industries of the National Accounts". That supports the NZSIOC-on-ANZSIC relationship but is a one-off conference paper, not the classification's defining document, and the branch rule since 2026-08-06 is that the corpus should not carry a node whose front matter nobody has read. One successful fetch of the DataInfo+ item closes this.
